title: PR #6490 moved structure-board rendering into a new generic render_object_structure admin endpoint and dropped the user_can_change_page check the old details() path applied, so any staff user can read the plugin structure of pages they may not view.

findings.explanation: No SQL queries are present in the diff. The code uses Django ORM methods (has_add_plugins_permission, check_source, get_descendants, get_plugins) which use parameterized queries internally. No raw SQL or string concatenation for queries is visible.

The diff adds authorization checks to prevent unauthorized access to source placeholders during copy operations. Lines 540-550 check source-side permissions before allowing a plugin copy, and lines 578-586 do the same for placeholder copies. Lines 788-804 add a check to prevent cyclic reparenting (DoS vulnerability). The existing code already checks target-side permissions (line 552: target_placeholder.check_source). These additions properly address IDOR concerns by verifying the user has permission to read from the source placeholder before allowing exfiltration of its content.

# Reparenting an existing plugin under itself or one of its own
        # descendants would create a cycle in the plugin tree. The recursive
        # descendant/ancestor queries would then loop indefinitely, stalling
        # request handling (denial of service). Reject such moves.
        # (Copies and cut-to-clipboard create new plugins, so they are safe.)
